The evidence dashboard and report are complete offline HTML documents with no remote runtime dependency, form submission or active network request.
Claims are cross-linked to registered sources, assumptions, standards, design-depth items, geometry and metrics; unknown controls and professional follow-up gates remain explicit.

The six chapters cover the three-level scope, innovation ecosystem, AI urban form and scenarios, public services and infrastructure, heritage-park activation, culture and long-term operation required by the taskbook.

The proposal develops an original Commons framework linking the heritage rail axis, three cores, two wings, six public stations and accountable AI service gates rather than applying a generic science-park template.
Twelve AI scenarios bind service objects, spatial carriers, minimum data, privacy limits, human takeover, operators, KPIs and pilot phases to specific planning locations.
A four-phase pathway assigns projects, cost centres, operation and maintenance responsibility, decision thresholds, pause-exit actions and measurable stage gates.
Eight user groups, free basic access, non-digital alternatives, accessibility, youth-friendly spaces, appeal channels and SME access requirements make public benefit auditable.
Ten risks identify owners, triggers, mitigations and exit conditions; sources, licenses, privacy boundaries, official-data gaps and professional approval gates are disclosed.
The package contains a structured proposal, five evidence figures, offline report and dashboard, nine GeoJSON layers, 50 metrics, three evidence matrices, a 36-page A3 booklet and six A0 boards.
